questions.question: What does it mean for two triangles to be congruent?
choices: Only their areas are equal
Corresponding sides and angles have equal measures
Only their angles are equal
Their side lengths share any scale factor

questions.question: Which condition is the SSS congruence criterion?
choices: Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal
Three pairs of corresponding angles are equal
Two sides and any angle are equal
One side and one angle are equal

questions.question: Which condition is the SAS congruence criterion?
choices: Two corresponding angles and any side are equal
Three corresponding angles are equal
Two corresponding sides and a nonincluded angle are equal
Two corresponding sides and their included angle are equal

questions.question: What does ASA require?
choices: Three corresponding angles
Two corresponding sides and the included angle
Two corresponding angles and the included side
One corresponding angle and one side

questions.question: Why is AAA alone insufficient to prove congruence?
choices: It never establishes similarity
It establishes shape but not size
It requires a right angle
It forces all sides to be equal

questions.question: Which special criterion applies to right triangles?
choices: Hypotenuse and one corresponding leg are equal
Any two corresponding angles are equal
Only the hypotenuses are equal
Only the areas are equal

questions.question: In triangle ABC congruent to triangle DEF, which side corresponds to AB?
choices: EF
DF
FE
DE

questions.question: What is an included angle between two sides?
choices: Any angle outside the triangle
The angle opposite both sides
The angle formed where those sides meet
An angle that must measure 90 degrees

questions.question: Two triangles have side lengths 4, 5, and 6 units. Why must they be congruent?
choices: The AAA criterion proves congruence
The SSS criterion applies
Equal perimeters always prove congruence
Any two triangles with a 4-unit side are congruent

questions.question: Two triangles have angles 40°, 60°, and 80° but different side lengths. What follows?
choices: They are similar but not congruent
They must be congruent
They cannot be similar
They must be right triangles

questions.question: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle RST. If angle B is 55°, what is angle S?
Which information is generally insufficient to prove two triangles congruent?
choices: Three corresponding sides
Two angles and their included side
Two sides and a nonincluded angle
Two sides and their included angle

questions.question: Two right triangles have hypotenuses of 13 units and one leg of 5 units. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: They are only similar because their sizes may differ
They are congruent by the hypotenuse-leg criterion
They are congruent by AAA alone
Their other legs may have different lengths

questions.question: If triangles are congruent, what can be concluded about their perimeters?
choices: Their perimeters are equal
Their perimeters differ by a factor of 2
Only their longest sides affect their perimeters
Their perimeters must be whole numbers

questions.question: Why does AAS prove congruence even though the known side is not between the two known angles?
choices: The known side becomes a hypotenuse
All three sides must be given first
AAS applies only to equilateral triangles
The third angle is fixed by the triangle angle sum

questions.question: Triangles ABC and ADC share side AC. If AB = AD and BC = DC, which criterion proves their congruence?
choices: ASA
AAA
SSS
Hypotenuse-leg only

questions.question: Triangles PQR and XYZ have PQ = XY, PR = XZ, and angle P = angle X. Which criterion applies?
choices: ASA
SAS
AAS
AAA

questions.question: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF with AB = 7, BC = 9, and AC = 11. What is the perimeter of triangle DEF?
choices: 27 units
18 units
22 units
20 units

questions.question: Two triangles each have sides of 6 and 8 units. One has an included angle of 40°, and the other has 70°. What can be concluded?
choices: They are congruent by SAS
They are congruent because two sides match
They are congruent by AAA
They are not congruent because the third side differs

questions.question: A diagonal splits a rectangle into two triangles. Which evidence proves their congruence by SSS?
choices: Both triangles have one right angle only
The diagonal has a positive length
Opposite rectangle sides are equal, and the diagonal is shared
The rectangle has four vertices
